A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same title, authors and research scope. All 32 pages of each version, including Appendices A–J, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original neural-network training experiments in Figures 1–6 and additional experiments and sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original training experiments and appendix analyses, including results on CIFAR-10 and Tiny Shakespeare.

M1.justification: The Frank–Wolfe pseudocode moves projection, per-restart scoring and maximum accumulation inside the restart loop, where v2 placed them outside. This changes the specified sharpness-estimation subroutine; the non-Euclidean GD update rules remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-10, CIFAR-10-5k and Tiny Shakespeare coverage, together with the same neural-network and quadratic-surrogate test scenarios.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added or removed. The generalized-versus-Euclidean sharpness comparisons in Figures E.3/G.5 and the RMSprop analysis in Appendix H are unchanged.

E3.justification: The written sharpness-measurement procedure changes: v2 scores the projected u_K, whereas v3 assigns the projection to u_K but scores d_K. This conflicts with the retained projection description. Other reported settings are unchanged, and no experimental rerun is established.

E4.justification: The pre-EoS oscillation analysis, fixed-direction curvature comparison, Frank–Wolfe restart sensitivity, Polar Express sensitivity, quadratic-surrogate tests and RMSprop parameter analysis are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Rendered comparisons establish that all empirical plots and their captions are identical, including the appendix figures. No result entries, numerical values, trajectories or reported qualitative findings change.

T1.justification: Equation (19) replaces the 2→2 norm label with ∞,2, matching the block norm already defined in v2 and used in Appendix I. This is a notation correction. The argmax edits are typographic; mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about directional smoothness, generalized sharpness, non-Euclidean EoS behavior and quadratic dynamics.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the restricted divergence guarantee, unexplained pre-EoS oscillations, sharpness-gap explanation and limitations of Frank–Wolfe estimation.

D1.justification: The algorithm listing revises implementation instructions through the loop correction and inconsistent u_K/d_K renaming. Appendix D retains the same implementation-source disclosure, full-batch setup, five restarts, 50 Frank–Wolfe iterations and five Polar Express steps.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to earlier EoS studies and non-Euclidean optimizers are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to notation, Algorithm 2-to-1 cross-references and the version/date stamp. There is no substantive prose rewrite or section reorganization.

P2.justification: The algorithm display is revised and renumbered, and its caption replaces the Equation (10) reference with an unexplained '(⋆)'. Equation typesetting causes small layout shifts. Empirical figures, axes, legends and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The restart-loop correction and consistent block-norm notation improve clarity. However, v3 introduces a mismatch between the projected u_K and the d_K used for scoring, contrary to the retained explanation, and replaces a usable equation reference with '(⋆)'. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these opposing effects on clarity and reproducibility do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
